transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-05
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Rivera (Redwood AE), Ethan Patel (Redwood CSM), Priya Anand (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (NovaOrbit Head of ML), Daniel Kim (NovaOrbit Platform), Sara Mbaye (NovaOrbit CTO)
---
Summary:
Brief QBR to review usage trends, costs, reliability incidents last quarter, roadmap alignment, and next steps around dedicated capacity for peak holiday batch processing. NovaOrbit is evaluating a move to a reserved pool for cost predictability; security/compliance items also requested.
Topics:
- Usage & cost trends (tokens, embeddings, peak days)
- Reliability incidents: 2 incident tickets in April (fallback behavior, region outage)
- Roadmap asks: longer context, streaming improvements, function/tool calling support
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, VPC/KMS requirements
---
Transcript:
[00:00] Marcus Rivera: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Marcus from Redwood, with Ethan and Priya. Hi NovaOrbit team.
[00:05] Lena Ortiz: Hi Marcus, hey all, thanks. Quick note, Sara might need to hop out at 15:45 pacific but should be here for the majority.
[00:12] Marcus: Got it. We'll try to do the exec bits early. Quick agenda, usage & cost, reliability review, roadmap asks, and then action items. Cool?
[00:20] Daniel Kim: Sounds good.
[00:22] Ethan Patel: I'll pull up the usage numbers I shared in the deck.
[00:27] Priya Anand: And I'll jump into a few infra notes on Dedicated sizing later.
[00:31] Marcus: Great. Ethan, you want to kick us off on usage?
[00:34] Ethan Patel: Yeah. So NovaOrbit, looking at the last 90 days, you've grown tokens ingested about 42% month-over-month, embeddings steady, chat gen is main driver. Peak day was May 12th — around 1.2M tokens/day, p95 latency on hosted api was about 420ms for the smaller models and 780ms for the larger curated model. Cost per 1k tokens for the larger model has been creeping up because of re-runs and some long-context workloads.
[01:05] Lena: That peak day was the promo push; we saw bursty traffic that stressed our pipelines, some timeouts at our edge.
[01:11] Marcus: Okay, that aligns with the incident notes — Priya you flagged two incidents, can you summarize?
[01:16] Priya Anand: Yeah. First incident April 13 — region failover caused a brief spike in retries; Redwood's smart routing fell back to a smaller capacity pool which increased token queuing and we hit the customer's retry threshold causing some duplicate requests. Second incident May 12 — sustained burst caused KV cache churn, which resulted in longer tail latency for sessions using long-context. We recommended increasing prefix cache TTL and a temporary autoscale bump. Both incidents resolved within 18-40 minutes.
[01:50] Daniel: We saw errors in our app logs during that time; our team tuned retry logic but want guarantees.
[01:56] Ethan: Understood — for guarantees we'd discuss Dedicated + SLA-backed latency which prevents noisy neighbor issues.
[02:02] Sara Mbaye: Quick Q — when you say Dedicated, does that include VPC with customer-managed KMS? Security is non-negotiable for us.
[02:10] Marcus: Yes, Redwood Private and Dedicated both have options. Dedicated includes reserved GPU pools; Private (VPC) supports customer KMS/HSM and audit logs. We'll share the SOC2/ISO pack.
[02:20] Sara: Ok good. Could you also confirm log retention and trace hooks? We need 12 months audit trail.
[02:26] Priya: Audit logs can be exported to your S3/GCS bucket for long-term retention; we also have per-route tracing in the console and can extend retention with the observability add-on.
[02:34] Lena: On costs — can you show the breakdown? We're seeing a big chunk from retries and high-context tokens.
[02:40] Ethan: Yep. The deck shows unit economics: ~62% of token cost last month was 1% of sessions that re-ran generation due to upstream timeouts, and long-context sessions (top 3% by length) account for 24% of token spend. We can recommend batching + prefix caching and a model quantization profile which reduces cost ~18% for those workloads.
[03:05] Marcus: On batching, are you doing continuous batching or client-side batch grouping?
[03:09] Daniel: We currently do client-side grouping of user messages into single requests, but not server-side batching.
[03:14] Priya: Redwood runtime supports continuous batching in Dedicated which helps throughput and lowers cost at the same latency SLO; we can show numbers in the dedicated planning session.
[03:23] Lena: What's the tradeoff for latency if we go quantized model? Our user SLO is 300ms p95.
[03:30] Priya: Quantization profiles can add approx 40-80ms p95 depending on model family; however combined with batching and caching you can often meet or beat current p95 cost-per-token. We should test with your seq len distribution.
[03:44] Sara: We're also evaluating Anthropic and Vertex AI; can you speak to Redwood's differentiation on reliability and rollout controls?
[03:52] Marcus: Sure — main differentiators: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private so rollouts and canary policies are consistent, and the console gives per-token visibility and rollback. We also have automatic fallback chains to lower-cost variants.
[04:05] Lena: Any customers in regulated finance using Dedicated with VPC in eu-west?
[04:10] Ethan: Yes, a couple — we can make an intro under NDA. They use our private control plane + KMS in-region.
[04:17] Daniel: On the technical side, we want to run a 2-week benchmark: 4k context generation at 100 concurrent streams. What's realistic?
[04:25] Priya: For that scale, Dedicated with streaming-optimized kernels and prewarm pool recommended. We'll size based on p50/p95 and token generation rate; prelim config is 4 A100-class GPUs per pool with autoscale. I'll propose exact numbers after we see your traffic profile.
[04:41] Marcus: Let's move to roadmap asks — Lena you sent a doc earlier about longer context and better function calling for structured outputs.
[04:48] Lena: Yes, our roadmap needs 8k context by Q4 and more deterministic function/tool calling for downstream-parser ingestion. Also improved streaming for partial tokens to reduce front-end wait.
[04:58] Priya: Internally we have kernel work targeting 16k sequences and streaming improvements; we can't commit exact dates but we can prioritize customers on dedicated trials.
[05:07] Sara: Are there charges for early access to those kernel improvements?
[05:11] Marcus: Typically early access is included as part of Dedicated trials or as an add-on for Private customers; we'll propose a pilot arrangement.
[05:18] Daniel: On SSO and RBAC — we need fine-grained role controls and SCIM.
[05:23] Ethan: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; RBAC currently supports route-level and team-level roles, and we're adding more granular token-level controls in the next release.
[05:33] Lena: Could you recap the incidents and mitigation steps you recommend so our infra team can implement quickly?
[05:40] Priya: Sure — 1) Increase prefix KV cache TTL and enable sticky routing for long sessions to reduce cache churn; 2) Adjust client-side retry/backoff thresholds to avoid duplicate replay; 3) Consider Dedicated reserved pool during your promo windows to avoid cross-tenant contention; 4) Export audit logs to your bucket for forensic analysis.
[06:02] Daniel: We'll try the retry tuning plus cache TTL change first. Who will own the cache TTL change?
[06:08] Priya: We can propose values — but your platform team will flip the config; we'll provide recommended settings and a rollout playbook.
[06:16] Marcus: Time check — about 25 minutes left. Any high level commercial asks?
[06:21] Sara: Budget review — we may need a committed reserved capacity quote for 500k tokens/day average with bursts to 1.5M.
[06:30] Marcus: We'll put together a reserved capacity quote with commitment tiers and burst options. That will include dedicated pool sizing and estimated unit cost.
[06:37] Lena: Also, can you run a cost model showing quantization vs non-quantized for our mix?
[06:42] Ethan: Yes, we'll run a comparative model using your token distribution and top-3 usage patterns.
[06:47] Marcus: Next, action items and owners — Ethan will send the usage report and QBR deck, Priya will draft dedicated sizing and playbook, Marcus will include pricing options, and Daniel will send traffic profile.
[06:58] Daniel: I'll export the session distribution csv today.
[07:02] Sara: One last security item — we need proof of key separation when using customer KMS. Is that in the SOC pack?
[07:08] Ethan: Yes, key separation and envelope encryption details are in the SOC2 + architectural security appendix; we'll send the link.
[07:15] Marcus: Great. Anything else?
[07:17] Lena: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.
[07:20] Marcus: Thanks — we'll follow up with the doc links and schedule dedicated planning.
